info.title: LiveLike Analytics API
info.description:
The LiveLike Analytics API gives you direct access to the data behind your LiveLike dashboards. It runs on top of [metabase.livelikecdn.com](https://metabase.livelikecdn.com), so the structure will feel familiar if you've worked with Metabase before.

## Core Concepts

### Collections
A Collection is a folder. It holds Cards, Dashboards, and Documents, and can be nested inside other Collections. Everything belongs to exactly one Collection. The root Collection (id `"root"`) sits at the top of the tree.

### Cards
A Card is a saved query with a chart. Each Card runs against one database, written in either raw SQL (`query_type: "native"`) or built with the query builder (`query_type: "query"`), and displays as a specific chart type — `scalar`, `table`, `bar`, `line`, `pie`, etc. Cards have filter slots (template-tag parameters) you fill in when downloading data.

### Dashboards
A Dashboard is a set of Cards on a canvas. Each Card placed on a Dashboard is called a Dashcard — it has its own `id` (`dashcard_id`) separate from the underlying Card's `id` (`card_id`). Dashboards can have filters that fan out to multiple Dashcards at once. To download data from a Dashboard Card you need three IDs: `dashboard_id`, `dashcard_id`, and `card_id`.

## Authentication
Every request needs an API key in the `x-api-key` header. Keys are scoped to specific Collections — requests outside that scope return `403 Forbidden`.

## Typical flow
1. **Find your Collection** — `GET /api/collection/tree` to browse the folder structure.
2. **List what's inside** — `GET /api/collection/{id}/items` to see the Cards and Dashboards in it.
3. **Check filters** — `GET /api/card/{id}` or `GET /api/dashboard/{id}` to see what parameters a Card or Dashboard takes.
4. **Download** — `POST /api/card/{id}/query/{format}` or `POST /api/dashboard/{dashboard_id}/dashcard/{dashcard_id}/card/{card_id}/query/{format}` with filter values in the body.

tags.name: Collections
tags.description:
Collections are folders that hold Cards, Dashboards, and Documents. They can be nested to any depth.

- Every Card and Dashboard belongs to exactly one Collection.
- The root Collection has `id: "root"` (a string, not an integer).
- The `location` field gives the full folder path, e.g. `"/11/74/"` means this Collection is inside 74, which is inside 11.
- Your API key only sees Collections it has been granted access to.
- Items with `is_personal: true` are individual user folders — skip these when looking for shared analytics content.
- Use `/api/collection/tree` for the full nested hierarchy. Use `/api/collection/` for a flat list. Use `/api/collection/{id}/items` to see what's inside a specific Collection.

tags.name: Cards
tags.description:
A Card is a single saved query with a chart. Every chart on a Dashboard and every standalone report you can download is backed by a Card.

- `query_type`: `"native"` = raw SQL, `"query"` = built with the query builder.
- `display`: the chart type — `scalar`, `table`, `bar`, `line`, `pie`, `row`, `area`, `combo`, `funnel`, `object`, etc.
- `parameters`: the filter slots on the Card. Pass values for these when downloading.
- `result_metadata`: the output columns. The `display_name` of each column is the key you'll get in JSON export rows.
- `database_id`: `3` = blast-prod PostgreSQL, `2` = Redshift analytics.
- `fully_parameterized: true` means all filters have defaults and the Card runs without you passing anything. If `false`, check `parameters[]` for entries where `required: true` and no `default` is set — those must be supplied or the download will fail.

tags.name: Dashboards
tags.description:
A Dashboard is a canvas of Cards, giving you a single view across multiple metrics with shared filter controls.

- A Dashboard holds one or more Dashcards — each one is a Card placed on the canvas.
- A Dashcard has two IDs: `id` (the `dashcard_id`, specific to this placement) and `card_id` (the underlying Card). You need both to download data via the Dashboard Card download endpoint.
- `parameters` on the Dashboard are the filter controls — things like a date range or a client selector. Some filter which rows are returned (e.g. `client_id`, `date_range`); others change the aggregation grain (e.g. an `interval` filter switching between `day`, `week`, `month`).
- `parameter_mappings` on each Dashcard shows how a dashboard filter maps to a template tag on that Card.
- `tabs`: present when the Dashboard uses a tabbed layout; each tab holds a subset of Dashcards.
- Always call `GET /api/dashboard/{id}` first — you need the `dashcard_id` and `card_id` from that response before hitting the download endpoint.

ApiKeyAuth.name: x-api-key
ApiKeyAuth.description: Your API key from LiveLike. It's scoped to specific Collections — requests to content outside its scope return `403 Forbidden`.

Collection.description: Metadata for a single Collection (folder). Use the `id` to list its contents via `GET /api/collection/{id}/items`.

id.description: The Collection ID. Regular collections use integers; the root collection uses the string `"root"`. Pass this as `collection_id` in follow-up requests.

description.description: Optional description. Null if not set.

slug.description: URL-safe version of the name. Null for the root Collection.

location.description: Folder path from root. `"/"` = direct child of root. `"/11/74/"` = inside Collection 74, which is inside 11.

is_personal.description: `true` for a user's personal folder. These aren't relevant for shared analytics — filter them out.

archived.description: `true` if archived (soft-deleted). Archived Collections are excluded from normal listings.

entity_id.description: A stable UUID that doesn't change on rename or move. Safe for long-lived references.

created_at.description: When the Collection was created, in ISO 8601 format.

children.description: The sub-collections nested inside this one. Only present in the `/api/collection/tree` response. An empty array means there are no sub-collections.

CollectionItem.description: A single item inside a Collection — either a Card, a Dashboard, or a Document.

id.description: The item's ID. For cards this is `card_id`; for dashboards this is `dashboard_id`.

name.description: The display name of the item.

model.description: Item type: `"card"` = saved query, `"dashboard"` = dashboard canvas, `"document"` = text notebook.

display.description: Chart type for Cards. Null for Dashboards and Documents.

description.description: Optional description. Null if not set.

collection_id.description: ID of the Collection this item belongs to.

database_id.description: Database the Card queries. Null for Dashboards and Documents. `2` = Redshift, `3` = blast-prod PostgreSQL.

entity_id.description: Stable UUID — doesn't change on rename or move.

last_used_at.description: Last time this item was viewed or run. Null if never used.

fully_parameterized.description: Cards only: `true` = all filters have defaults, safe to call with `parameters: []`. `false` = at least one filter has no default — check `parameters[]` before downloading. Always `false` for Dashboards; ignore it there.

CollectionItemsResponse.description: The paginated response you get back from `GET /api/collection/{id}/items`.

total.description: Total number of matching items across all pages. Can be null when the Collection is empty.

data.description: The items on the current page.

models.description: Which item types are included in this response, e.g. `["card", "dashboard"]`.

limit.description: How many items per page were requested.

offset.description: The zero-based starting position used for this page.

TemplateTagParameter.description: A filter slot on a Card. Maps to a `{{variable_name}}` placeholder in SQL or a filter widget in the query builder.

name.description: Internal name — matches `{{variable_name}}` in the SQL. Use this in `target` arrays when querying.

required.description: `true` means you must include this parameter in the download request body. If `required` is `true` and no `default` is set, calling the download endpoint without it will return a `400 Bad Request` or trigger a `500` query error. Always check this field before calling the download endpoint.

default.description: Default value when nothing is passed. When set, the Card runs without that parameter.

ResultMetadataColumn.description: Metadata for a single output column in the Card's query results.

name.description: Raw column name from the query.

display_name.description: Column header in the UI — and the exact key in JSON export rows.

semantic_type.description: Optional semantic label, e.g. `"type/PK"`, `"type/FK"`. Null if not set.

CardMetadata.description:
Metadata for a Card — no query is run. Use this to check what filters a Card needs and what columns it returns before hitting the download endpoint.

If `fully_parameterized` is `false`, look through `parameters[]` for entries where `required: true` and no `default` — those must be included in the download request body.

description.description: What the Card measures. Null if not set.

query_type.description: `"native"` = raw SQL. `"query"` = built with the query builder.

database_id.description: Database this Card queries. `2` = Redshift, `3` = blast-prod PostgreSQL.

entity_id.description: Stable UUID — survives renames and moves.

created_at.description: When the Card was created, in ISO 8601 format.

updated_at.description: When the Card's query or settings were last changed, in ISO 8601 format.

parameters.description: Filter slots on this Card. Pass values for these in the download request body. Empty array = no filters.

result_metadata.description: Output columns from the last successful run. `display_name` is the key in JSON export rows.

DashboardParameter.description:
A filter at the Dashboard level — e.g. a date range or client selector. Values passed here flow to all wired Dashcards via `parameter_mappings`.

Not all filters narrow rows — some change the aggregation grain (e.g. an `interval` filter with values `day`, `week`, `month`). Check `slug` and `type` to understand what a filter does.

default.description: Default value when nothing is passed.

ParameterMapping.description: Links a dashboard filter to a template tag on a Dashcard. Metabase uses this to inject the filter value into the Card's query.

parameter_id.description: UUID of the dashboard filter driving this mapping.

target.description: Points to the template tag on the Card, e.g. `["variable", ["template-tag", "client_id"]]`.

DashboardCard.description: A Card placed on a Dashboard canvas (Dashcard). Has its own `id` (`dashcard_id`) separate from the underlying `card_id`. You need both for the download endpoint.

id.description: Dashcard ID — specific to this Card placement on the Dashboard. Pass as `dashcard_id` in the download endpoint.

card_id.description: Card ID — the underlying Card. Pass as `card_id` in the download endpoint.

parameter_mappings.description: How dashboard filters map to this Card's template tags. Empty array = no dashboard filters wired to this Dashcard.

DashboardTab.description: A tab in a tabbed Dashboard.

Dashboard.description: Full Dashboard metadata including all Dashcards and filters. Call this before downloading — you need `dashcard_id` and `card_id` from `dashcards[]`.

description.description: What the Dashboard shows. Null if not set.

entity_id.description: Stable UUID — survives renames and moves.

created_at.description: When the Dashboard was created, in ISO 8601 format.

updated_at.description: When the Dashboard layout or settings were last changed, in ISO 8601 format.

parameters.description: Dashboard-level filters. Pass values here to filter all wired Dashcards at once. Some filters narrow rows (client, date); others change aggregation grain (e.g. interval: `day`/`week`/`month`).

tabs.description: Tabs in a tabbed Dashboard. Empty array = single pane with no tabs.

dashcards.description: All Cards on this Dashboard. Each entry has the `dashcard_id` and `card_id` needed for the download endpoint.

QueryFilterParameter.description: A filter value for a Card's template tag. Add one per filter slot you want to set.

type.description: Filter type. `"category"` for text tags. Other common values: `"number/="`, `"date/single"`, `"date/range"`.

target.description: Points to the template tag. Format: `["variable", ["template-tag", "<tag_name>"]]` — `<tag_name>` matches the `name` in the Card's `parameters` array.

parameters.description: Filter values to apply. Pass `[]` if the Card has no required filters or you're using defaults. Add one entry per filter you want to set. Omitting a `required: true` parameter with no `default` returns a `400` or `500`.

ExportJsonRow.description: One row from a JSON export. Keys are the `display_name` values from `result_metadata`. Value types vary by column.

get.description:
Returns a flat list of all Collections your API key has access to. Use the `id` values to list what's inside with `GET /api/collection/{id}/items`.

Use `/api/collection/tree` instead when you need the full nested hierarchy in one call.

> **Note:** The root Collection has `id: "root"` (a string). All others use integer IDs.

> **Tip:** Filter out items where `is_personal: true` — these are individual user folders, not shared analytics content.

200.description: A flat array of Collections visible to your API key.

OK.summary: Two collections — root and a top-level analytics collection

401.description: Unauthorized — `x-api-key` header is missing or invalid.

get.description:
Returns the full Collection hierarchy as a nested tree. Each Collection has a `children` array containing its sub-collections recursively.

Useful for building navigation or finding a deeply nested Collection by name without having to reconstruct the tree from `location` paths.

> **Tip:** `entity_id` stays stable across renames and moves — safer to store than `id` or `slug`.

200.description: An array of top-level Collections, each with a recursive `children` array.

OK.summary: Top-level collection with one nested sub-collection

401.description: Unauthorized — `x-api-key` header is missing or invalid.

get.description:
Lists the Cards, Dashboards, and Documents inside a Collection. Use `models` to filter by type, and `limit`/`offset` to page through large Collections.

- Cards (`model: "card"`) → use `id` as `card_id` in `GET /api/card/{id}` and the Card download endpoint.
- Dashboards (`model: "dashboard"`) → use `id` as `dashboard_id` in `GET /api/dashboard/{id}` and the Dashboard download endpoint.

> **Note:** `total` can be null when the Collection is empty. Check `data.length` instead.

parameters.name: collection_id
parameters.description: An integer Collection ID from `GET /api/collection/` or `GET /api/collection/tree`. Don't pass the string `"root"` here — you need an actual integer ID.

parameters.name: models
parameters.description: Filter by item type. Repeat to include multiple: `?models=card&models=dashboard`. Leave it out to get everything.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max items per page. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Where to start in the list (zero-based). Use with `limit` to page through: second page = `offset=50`, third = `offset=100`, and so on.

200.description: A paginated list of items in the Collection.

OK.summary: Mixed cards and dashboard in a collection

401.description: Unauthorized — `x-api-key` header is missing or invalid.

403.description: Forbidden — your API key doesn't have access to this Collection.

get.description:
Returns the full metadata for a Card without running the query. Call this before downloading to check what filters are needed and what columns come back.

- `parameters` — filter slots and whether they're required.
- `result_metadata` — output columns; use `display_name` as the key in JSON exports.
- `fully_parameterized` — `true` means you can call the download endpoint with `parameters: []`. If `false`, check `parameters[]` for entries where `required: true` and no `default` — those must be passed or the download fails.

> **Tip:** `display_name` values in `result_metadata` are the exact keys in JSON export rows.

parameters.name: card_id
parameters.description: Card ID from `GET /api/collection/{id}/items` — look for items where `model` is `"card"`.

200.description: Full Card metadata including parameters and result_metadata.

ScalarCard.summary: Scalar card with no required parameters

FilteredTableCard.summary: Table card requiring a client_id filter

value.name: Total Distinct Users
value.description: Counts unique user profiles that have interacted with at least one widget.

401.description: Unauthorized — `x-api-key` header is missing or invalid.

403.description: Forbidden — your API key doesn't have access to this Card.

post.description:
Runs the Card's query and returns results in the format you choose.

Check `fully_parameterized` first. If `false`, call `GET /api/card/{id}` and look for `required: true` parameters with no `default` — you must include those in the request body.

**Request body:** `parameters` array with one entry per filter you want to set. Pass `[]` if there are no required filters.

**JSON format:** flat array of objects — keys are `display_name` values from `result_metadata`.

| Format | Use for |
|--------|----------|
| `json` | Processing in code |
| `csv` | Spreadsheets or pipelines |
| `xlsx` | Excel files for end users |

> This is a `POST`, not a `GET` — filter values go in the request body.

parameters.name: export_format
parameters.description: The format you want back. `csv` → `text/csv`. `json` → `application/json` (flat array of row objects). `xlsx` → Excel spreadsheet (`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`).

NoFilters.summary: No filters — Card runs with defaults

MultipleFilters.summary: Filter by both client_id and a date range

200.description: Query results in the format you requested.

400.description: Bad Request — the JSON body is malformed or a required filter parameter is missing from the `parameters` array.

401.description: Unauthorized — `x-api-key` header is missing or invalid.

403.description: Forbidden — your API key doesn't have access to this Card.

500.description: Query failed — the Card's SQL threw a database error. This often means a required template tag parameter was not passed or was set to an invalid value. Check `parameters[]` on the Card and ensure all entries with `required: true` are included.

get.description:
Returns full Dashboard metadata — all Dashcards, filter controls, and layout. Call this before downloading Dashboard Card data to get the `dashcard_id` and `card_id` you need.

1. Find the Card you want in `dashcards[]` by `card.name`, then note its `id` (dashcard_id) and `card_id`.
2. Check `parameters` — if filters exist, you can pass values in download requests.
3. `dashcards[].parameter_mappings` shows which dashboard filter maps to which template tag on each Card.
4. `tabs` — non-empty means the Dashboard has a tabbed layout.

parameters.name: dashboard_id
parameters.description: Dashboard ID from `GET /api/collection/{id}/items` — look for items where `model` is `"dashboard"`.

200.description: Dashboard metadata with the full Dashcard list.

OK.summary: Arcade Games dashboard with two dashcards

DashboardWithFilters.summary: Dashboard with a client_id filter wired to all dashcards

value.name: Client Overview
value.description: Cross-feature KPIs scoped to a single client.

401.description: Unauthorized — `x-api-key` header is missing or invalid.

403.description: Forbidden — your API key doesn't have access to this Dashboard.

post.description:
Runs the query for a specific Card inside a Dashboard and returns results in the format you choose. Use this instead of the standalone Card download when the Card is on a Dashboard — it respects the Dashboard's filter wiring.

You need three IDs from `GET /api/dashboard/{dashboard_id}`:
- `dashboard_id` — from `GET /api/collection/{id}/items`
- `dashcard_id` — from `dashcards[].id`
- `card_id` — from `dashcards[].card_id`

To apply dashboard filters, build `QueryFilterParameter` entries using the `target` from the Dashcard's `parameter_mappings`.

> This is a `POST`, not a `GET` — filter values go in the request body.

parameters.name: dashboard_id
parameters.description: Dashboard ID from `GET /api/collection/{id}/items` — look for items where `model` is `"dashboard"`.

parameters.name: dashcard_id
parameters.description: Dashcard ID from `GET /api/dashboard/{id}` → `dashcards[].id`. This is the placement ID — not the same as `card_id`.

parameters.name: card_id
parameters.description: Card ID from `GET /api/dashboard/{id}` → `dashcards[].card_id`. This is the underlying question ID.

parameters.name: export_format
parameters.description: The format you want back. `csv` → `text/csv`. `json` → `application/json` (flat array of row objects). `xlsx` → Excel spreadsheet.

NoFilters.summary: No filters — Card runs with defaults

MultipleFilters.summary: Filter by client_id and date range

200.description: Query results in the format you requested.

400.description: Bad Request — the JSON body is malformed or a required filter parameter is missing.

401.description: Unauthorized — `x-api-key` header is missing or invalid.

403.description: Forbidden — your API key doesn't have access to this Dashboard or Card.

404.description: Dashboard, Dashcard, or Card not found. Double-check all three IDs from `GET /api/dashboard/{id}`.

500.description: Query failed — the underlying SQL threw a database error. Make sure all required template tag parameters are present and set to valid values.
